items.t: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
items.d: The AI company is expected to set its valuation range this week, the Wall Street Journal reported.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 5:27 PM PST · November 9, 2026 Image Credits: Ruhani Kaur/Bloomberg / Getty Images Marina Temkin Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans Launching a major tech IPO would seem risky right now, shortly after one of Nasdaq’s biggest sell-offs and amid revelations that a CEO central to the AI boom had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But that isn’t deterring Anthropic, which is moving ahead with its listing plans, according to The Wall Street Journal . Anthropic plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, the Journal reported. Investors will look to Anthropic’s valuation to gauge the strength of the AI boom. Some institutional investors are now pushing for a valuation below the $1.5 trillion target discussed as recently as last week, a figure that was itself considerably below the $2 trillion floated a few months ago, the report said. OpenAI, Anthropic’s main rival, was reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion last week after the ChatGPT maker raised $11 billion in fresh capital, short of the $20 billion it had initially sought. items.d: The Nvidia CEO also pulled out of an Anthropic event earlier.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 12:09 PM PST · November 9, 2026 Image Credits: Jose Sarmento Matos/Bloomberg / Getty Images Ivan Mehta Jensen Huang pulls out of ElevenLabs Summit amid Nvidia controversy Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pulled out of the ElevenLabs Summit scheduled for this Wednesday in New York, ElevenLabs, the voice AI company, confirmed Monday. He has also dropped out of other speaking engagements, including the Anthropic CEO Forum . Nvidia is an investor in ElevenLabs. The withdrawals come after Huang admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and Nvidia opened an investigation into his relationship with a possible Chinese spy. “I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang said in a memo to the company. The incident has rattled the AI industry, raising questions about Huang’s staying power as CEO and Nvidia’s own China ambitions. items.t: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
items.d: Anthropic says the new models "show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision," as well as in communicating more clearly with users.
items.fullText: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. The company says the new models “show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision” and communicate more clearly with users. Notably, Anthropic is lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. As a result, Fable 5.2 is now cheaper than its primary competitor GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic says that the new version of Fable will return responses 30% faster across effort levels. Faster inference serving is available for double the price. Fable 5.2 is also compatible with zero data retention (ZDR) policies through the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards system , long a sticking point for many enterprise clients. It’s Anthropic’s first model release since the arrival of a third-party report from the assessment group METR , which suggested the lab might be approaching recursive self-improvement (RSI) — or the ability for AI models to carry on model training independently. The METR report found internal models were speeding up Anthropic’s AI progress by roughly 2x, although many uncertainties remain. Still, Anthropic’s release notes significant ongoing challenges in accurately testing model capabilities. “Claude Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 each voice suspicion that they are being evaluated more often than any of our recent models, which challenges our ability to assess how they will act in real-world settings. items.t: Anthropic joins AI’s natural gas frenzy, buys $3.4B worth of turbines
items.d: Anthropic bought billions of dollars' worth of natural gas turbines in a deal that could give it buyer's remorse.
items.fullText: AI’s power crunch has become so acute that Anthropic, a company that has generally avoided buying physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines. The AI company, which is planning to go public this year, is buying Caterpillar generators that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered, according to a Financial Times report . The generators are capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity. Historically, Anthropic has preferred to rent rather than buy. The company disclosed in its S-1 filing in May that it is paying SpaceX subsidiary xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 to use xAI’s computing power. “We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts,” Anthropic stated in the filing, meaning more deals to rent computing power. But as demand for compute ramps up, the market for power has also grown increasingly uncertain, which may have forced its hand. The backlog for natural gas turbines stretches into the early 2030s, and queues to connect to the electrical grid can be just as long. Anthropic’s purchase looks like a last resort. According to the report, OnePWR ordered the turbines a couple years ago but couldn’t find financing to complete the purchase. Anthropic had planned to buy them from OnePWR but instead went directly to Caterpillar, the manufacturer. It’s not clear why OnePWR was unable to secure financing despite Anthropic’s apparent interest as a customer. Whatever the case, Anthropic likely wanted to keep the generating capacity to itself rather than give a competitor an opportunity to snap it up. AI companies have been ramping up their purchases of natural gas equipment and supplies in recent years. Google , Amazon , Microsoft , and Meta have all announced plans to build massive natural gas power plants to power their data centers on-site, rather than drawing from the public grid. November 8, 2026 by Nicola Sessions 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them. Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows . A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions. AIM Intelligence , a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage. The company is also considering a preliminary proof of concept for the public energy sector, with potential applications across enterprise, industrial and robotics environments. On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea . Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts. NVIDIA Nemotron is a family of open models, datasets and techniques that help developers build specialized, efficient AI agents. items.fullText: Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents November 5, 2026 by Hannah Coutand 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action. Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task. As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power. What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt. Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity. The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Vera delivers industry-leading agent speed while enabling 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fastest x86 CPU. Vera delivers 2x faster agent speed with leading energy efficiency compared with the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Partners are already putting Vera to work. Early adopters see the same exceptional performance in production-style tests: Perplexity : Ran agentic coding tasks 1.5x faster with Vera than on traditional CPUs. Perplexity plans to deploy Vera in an upcoming production system. items.fullText: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models With a parakeet, a webcam and a conviction that AI belongs to everyone — how one NVIDIAN became NVIDIA Nemotron’s loudest advocate. November 5, 2026 by Matthew Leib 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Chris Alexiuk has a simple rule about open source AI: If you believe in it, be loud about it. “We should be shouting about this technology from the rooftops,” said Alexiuk, a Toronto-based senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in making open large language models (LLMs) practical for working developers. Alexiuk’s preferred “rooftop” is YouTube , where he’s built a following teaching curious thousands how to build, fine-tune, evaluate and ship production LLM applications and agents. “I think the people who will most help us understand how to build and apply AI likely haven’t even heard of it yet,” he said. “Trying to get knowledge and information out to as many people as humanly possible is what continues to drive me.” Bringing NVIDIA Nemotron to Developers Everywhere Having spent years teaching developers to build with open models, Alexiuk has concluded that transparency isn’t a feature of good AI; it’s the precondition for it. “Fully open source AI is necessary for the democratization of intelligence,” he said. “You should have access to the weights, the data that went into it, the training recipes, everything.” That’s why, on his LinkedIn profile, Alexiuk styles himself “No. 1 Nemotron Fan,” referring to the NVIDIA Nemotron family of open source, multimodal models built for long-running, self-evolving and specialized AI agents. “I think Nemotron is the most important project that exists,” said Alexiuk, who also uses the pseudonym “Joe Nemotron” across social media. “I’m a firm believer that openness is a very important thing to undertake, so I’m going to be the No. 1 fan of whoever is doing that the best. items.fullText: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge November 5, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack. But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory. That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit. How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed. Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it. From NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose roughly 3%, while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX. Agentic Inference Is Putting More Pressure on HBM Frontier models now have trillions of parameters — the values that hold what an AI model learned in training. KV cache, which holds the context the model needs to understand each active request without reprocessing the same information, is also expanding. items.fullText: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI From infrastructure planning and transportation to public services, cities are using NVIDIA-powered applications to address local needs and expand capacity for the broader AI ecosystem. November 2, 2026 by Esther Lee 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge. Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used. Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own. Agentic AI for Cities From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough. In Spain, 1MillionBot combines open source ALIA models trained at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with NVIDIA Nemotron and other models in resident-service agents for Madrid Digital (Comunidad de Madrid), Administració Oberta de Catalunya and 150+ deployments across Spain, handling municipal procedures, appointment requests, urban-planning incidents and service inquiries. items.fullText: 삼성, 샘 올트먼과 ‘AI 혁신’ 간담회 개최 ‘AI Driven’ 경영 강화… 전사적 AX 추진 가속 2026/10/31 AI 요약 새로운 뉴스룸 AI 기능을 살펴보세요! 닫기 --> AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 삼성, 샘 올트먼 CEO 초청해 AI 시대 미래 경영 전략 논의 삼성은 31일 경기도 용인 삼성인력개발원에서 삼성전자 등 주요 관계사 사장단을 대상으로 샘 올트먼(Sam Altman) OpenAI CEO 초청 간담회를 개최했다. 이날 간담회에는 전자·금융·바이오 등 삼성 관계사 사장단 50여 명이 참석했으며, 샘 올트먼 CEO와 함께 ‘AI가 바꿀 다음 10년, 기업의 선택’을 주제로 진행됐다. 삼성 사장단과 샘 올트먼 CEO는 AI 기술의 발전 방향과 활용 가능성을 살펴보고, 이를 바탕으로 새롭게 형성될 시장과 사업 기회에 대한 의견을 나눴다. 또한 AI가 기업의 의사결정과 조직 운영에 미칠 영향을 짚어보며, 새로운 경영 환경에서 경영진이 갖춰야 할 역량에 대해서도 소통했다. 삼성은 전사적 AX 추진을 위한 사장단 교육의 일환으로 경영진의 AI 이해도를 높이고 미래 경영 전략을 모색하기 위해 이번 간담회를 마련했다. 삼성은 글로벌 AI 혁신을 주도하는 OpenAI의 CEO를 초청하는 등 AI 시대의 변화에 선제적으로 대응하고 미래 경쟁력을 강화하는 데 힘을 쏟고 있다. AI 시대의 경쟁력이 경영진의 판단력과 실행력에서 비롯된다는 인식 아래, 사장단이 앞장서 AI를 배우고 활용하는 문화를 확산시키고 있다. 삼성전자와 OpenAI는 지난해 10월 글로벌 AI 인프라 구축을 위한 협력 의향서(LOI)를 체결하고, OpenAI의 스타게이트 프로젝트에 필요한 메모리 반도체 공급을 추진해 왔다. 당시 삼성SDS는 AI 데이터센터 구축과 기업용 AI 서비스 분야에서 협력하기로 했으며, 삼성물산과 삼성중공업은 해상 부유식 데이터센터 공동 개발을 진행하기로 했다. 올해 7월에는 이재용 삼성전자 회장이 미국 샌프란시스코 OpenAI 본사를 방문하는 등 양사 간 교류도 지속해 왔다. 삼성 사장단, 지난 6월에 이어 생성형 AI 집중교육 추가 진행 삼성 사장단은 이날 샘 올트먼 CEO와의 간담회에 앞서 생성형 AI 실습 교육을 진행했다. 지난 6월 사장단을 대상으로 첫 AI 집중교육을 실시한 데 이어, 4개월 만에 시행된 추가 교육이다. 삼성은 사장단부터 AI 기술을 직접 익히고 업무에 적용할 수 있도록 교육 프로그램을 지속 운영하고 있으며, 이를 실제 활용할 수 있는 능력을 높이는 데 초점을 맞췄다. 사장단은 흩어진 경영 자료를 AI로 정리해 자신만의 ‘지식저장소’를 구성하고, 의사결정에 AI를 활용하는 역량을 높였다. 삼성, ‘AI Driven’ 경영 본격화… 전사적 AI 대전환 추진 삼성은 지난 6월부터 연구개발에서 생산·마케팅·지원 업무까지 전 분야에 AI를 도입하는 ‘AI 대전환’을 본격 추진하고 있다. AI를 활용해 업무 생산성과 사업 경쟁력을 높이고, 제품과 서비스는 물론 기업 운영 전반에 AI를 접목해 나갈 계획이다. 이를 위해 관계사별 사업 특성과 업무 환경에 맞는 AI 활용 방안을 마련하고, 임직원들이 AI를 적극적으로 활용할 수 있는 기반을 확대하고 있다. 지난 6월 사장단 교육을 시작으로 약 2,300명의 임원을 대상으로 교육을 추진했으며, 교육 대상을 일반 직원까지 확대해 2027년 2월까지 전 임직원 대상 AI 교육을 완료한다는 목표를 제시했다. 삼성은 관계사별 AI 전담조직을 구축하고, 외부 생성형 AI 서비스의 업무 활용도 확대하고 있다. AI 전담조직은 각 회사의 사업 특성에 맞는 AX 전략을 수립하고, 데이터와 AI 모델의 운영 및 활용을 지원하는 역할을 한다. 삼성은 앞으로 AI 기술의 발전과 산업 환경 변화에 선제적으로 대응하는 한편, 관계사별 AX 추진 성과를 지속 점검하고 실행 과제를 구체화해 AI 중심의 경영 체계를 정착시

items.fullText: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals Scientists at the Allen Telescope Array have integrated the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to search for signals that may come from aliens — or the AI they built. October 30, 2026 by Chris Porter 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens. Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI. Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on. The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies. “As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear.
